title: Finite-range comparison
statement: Let $\square=(f,f',g,g',\alpha)$ be a cartesian square of schemes [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square], with $f:X\to Y$, $g:Y'\to Y$, $f':X'\to Y'$, $g':X'\to X$. All coefficients are abelian groups: let $K\in D^+(\Ab(X_{\Et}))$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], and let $a\le b$ be integers with $\mathcal H^q(K)=0$ for $q\notin[a,b]$. Write $\Phi=g^{-1}Rf_*$, $\Psi=Rf'_*g'^{-1}$ and $\Ex_\square:\Phi\to\Psi$ for the derived exchange transformation [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange]. Let $\varphi$ be the spectral-sequence morphism induced by $\Ex_\square$ on the two truncation couples [def-weil-pbc-truncation-exact-couples], whose spectral sequences are (2) and (3) of [def-weil-pbc-hypercohomology-filtrations]. If $\varphi_2^{p,q}:g^{-1}R^pf_*\mathcal H^q(K)\to R^pf'_*g'^{-1}\mathcal H^q(K)$ is an isomorphism for every $(p,q)$, then $\varphi_\infty^{p,q}$ and the induced map $\mathcal H^n(\Ex_{\square,K}):\mathcal H^n(g^{-1}Rf_*K)\to\mathcal H^n(Rf'_*g'^{-1}K)$ are isomorphisms for every $(p,q)$ and every $n$. Consequently $\Ex_{\square,K}$ is an isomorphism. In the generic abelian-coefficient notation this is $\operatorname{IsIso}((\operatorname{Etale.derivedBaseChangeMapPlus}\ \Ab\ \mathsf{sq.toCommSq}).\operatorname{app}K)$, where $\mathsf{sq}:\operatorname{IsPullback}(g\prime,f\prime,f,g)$ witnesses the same square and $K$ is viewed in $\mathrm{DerivedCategory.Plus}(\mathrm{Sheaf}(X_{\Et},\Ab))$.

proof.text: Use lem-weil-pbc-truncation-couple-morphism to obtain the two exact couples with all ten data identifications and the three exchange squares. Conjugate tD and tE by the recorded D and E equalities; family_conj converts the heterogeneous structure-map identifications into these conjugation formulas. The squares then give the hypotheses of lem-sp-couple-morphism, whose pages have initial map the transported tE and whose successor maps satisfy the kernel and cokernel squares.

proof.text: The hypothesis on cohomology outside [a,b] gives vanishing below a. Apply lemma-weil-pbc-exact-couple-abutment to the recorded couples. Its four half-plane bounds permit the convergence clause of lem-sp-couple-morphism, giving one pair of limiting subobjects and the globally indexed limiting maps required in the conclusion. For each cohomological degree n, apply the abutment theorem again for its own finite filtrations, their canonical identifications, and the exchange-induced graded comparison. Neither the upper bound b nor a <= b is needed for this argument.

proof.text: Prove page induction directly in the exact-couple page API (private helpers page_kernel_isIso, page_maps_isIso, limit_transport, restriction_iso, and limit_map_isIso). At a successor the isomorphisms on page objects induce an isomorphism on outgoing kernels; the incoming differential and its kernel lift then give an isomorphism on cokernels, which is the next page map by the quotient square. Both the page maps and their inverses satisfy differential and successor-projection compatibility. Use the existing exactCoupleFiniteTransport theorem of lem-sp-derived-couple-functoriality in both directions to preserve the recursive finite cycles and boundaries. Reuse transport_square from Sheaf.CategoryTheory.ExactFunctorHalfPlane with the identity functor for the elementary equality reindexing, and the factors_iff_image_le helper from DerivedCoupleFunctoriality when passing to limiting cycles. The greatest-lower-bound and least-upper-bound properties give preservation of limiting cycles and boundaries. Restrict the initial map and its inverse to get inverse maps on those subobjects. The two limiting cokernel squares identify any supplied limiting map with the induced cokernel isomorphism. Apply this to the global limiting map and to each degree-specific abutment limiting map. This is the usual page-comparison argument, using the existing finite transport theorem and local isomorphism helpers without converting the couples to Mathlib spectral sequences.

proof.text: In degree n, use the abutment theorem to obtain the two finite image filtrations U and V on the actual cohomology objects, the restrictions of cohomology of exchange, and its graded maps. The private finite_image helper transports finite bounds along the canonical abutment isomorphisms. The canonical graded comparison square expresses each graded map as the limiting isomorphism of Step 3 conjugated by the two comparison isomorphisms. The private filtered_iso_of_graded helper identifies the supplied restriction and graded maps with those in lem-sp-finite-filtration-induction by monomorphism and cokernel-epimorphism cancellation, then applies that theorem. This proves that every cohomology map of the same exchange component is invertible.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-derived-stalk-conservative] on $Y'$ to $\Ex_{\square,K}:\Phi K\to\Psi K$, whose two objects are bounded below as in [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange]. It gives that $\Ex_{\square,K}$ itself is an isomorphism.

old_proof.text: Construct $t_D^{p,q}=\mathcal H^{p+q}(\Ex_{\square,\tau_{\le q}K})$ and $t_E^{p,q}=\mathcal H^{p+q}(\Ex_{\square,\mathcal H^q(K)[-q]})$. By [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-couple-morphism], both truncation couples are exact and these maps commute with all three structure maps, including the boundary. They therefore satisfy the exact-couple-morphism hypotheses of [lem-sp-couple-morphism], which gives compatible maps on every spectral-sequence page, not merely unrelated maps between entries. Clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-couple-morphism] identifies the initial components with the stated degree-$p$ exchange maps of $\mathcal H^q(K)$. Thus this constructed morphism is the $\varphi$ in the hypothesis.

source.place: Proof: the comparison of the two hypercohomology spectral sequences, constructed explicitly

old_proof.text: The bound $\mathcal H^q(K)=0$ outside $[a,b]$ implies the lower bound $q<a$ required by [lemma-weil-pbc-exact-couple-abutment]. Apply that lemma to the two couples and the map just constructed. Its clause (1) verifies $D^{p,q}=0$ for $q<a$ and $E_2^{p,q}=0$ unless $p\ge0$ and $q\ge a$, exactly the half-plane hypotheses required by [lem-sp-couple-morphism]. It supplies finite canonical abutment filtrations and existing limiting pages. Clause (2) supplies the isomorphisms $\iota_n:D^{0,n}\to\mathcal H^n(\Phi K)$ and $\iota'_n:D'^{0,n}\to\mathcal H^n(\Psi K)$ carrying these finite filtrations to the image filtrations on the desired abutments. Only finitely many $q\in[a,b]$ can contribute in total degree $n$; if $n<a$, all those terms are zero.

source.place: Proof: finite filtration on each abutment and the bounds

old_proof.text: Apply [lem-sp-page-induction] to the spectral-sequence morphism of Step 1, in the abelian category $\Ab(Y'_{\Et})$: the hypothesis supplies isomorphisms on every $E_2$ component, and Step 2 supplies the existing limiting pages. Hence every finite-page component and every $E_\infty$ component is an isomorphism. Explicitly, the page induction starts with $\varphi_2$; at a successor the componentwise inverse of $\varphi_r$ commutes with the differential because $\varphi_r d_r=d'_r\varphi_r$, so it is an inverse map of page complexes. Homology and the compatible page-to-page isomorphisms give an inverse for $\varphi_{r+1}$. The cycle and boundary subobjects defining the limiting pages are carried isomorphically by these maps. This direct page-comparison lemma has no directed-colimit hypotheses and needs no singleton-index construction.

old_proof.text: For fixed $n$, clause (3) of [lemma-weil-pbc-exact-couple-abutment] gives $\iota'_n\circ t_D^{0,n}=\mathcal H^n(\Ex_{\square,K})\circ\iota_n$. Its clause (4) says that $u_n=\mathcal H^n(\Ex_{\square,K})$ respects every step of the image filtrations and that its graded maps are precisely $\varphi_\infty^{p,n-p}$ under the canonical identifications. Thus $u_n$ is a morphism of the finite filtered abutments of Step 2, and all its graded maps are isomorphisms by Step 3. All hypotheses of [lem-sp-finite-filtration-induction] are now supplied, so $u_n$ is an isomorphism for each $n$ (no strictness hypothesis is needed).

old_proof.text: Identify the arrow, rather than just its source and target. By [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange], $\Ex_{\square,K}$ is the composite of the unit $\eta_{f',g^{-1}Rf_*K}$, the square transport $Rf'_*\theta^D_{\square,Rf_*K}$, and the counit map $Rf'_*g'^{-1}\varepsilon_{f,K}$. In exact master MorphismDefs.lean, Etale.baseChange_app expands the component into baseChangeUnitStep, baseChangeSquareStep and baseChangeCounitStep. Their component formulas are respectively these same unit, square transport, and counit, with $A=\Ab$ and the commutative-square proof $\mathsf{sq.toCommSq}$. The termwise exact abelian inverse images of [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image] are the master's derived upper-star functors. Thus the composite equals the master component, on the same $K$, from $g^{-1}Rf_*K$ to $Rf'_*g'^{-1}K$. No $\operatorname{ModuleCat}\Lambda$ transformation is substituted. If one uses the alternate square notation of sbc-def-base-change-map, its letters must be renamed $(T,S,X,Y;g,f,e,h)=(X,Y,Y',X';f,g,g',f')$, so the old subscript would be $\operatorname{BC}_{g,f}$; the statement instead names the master arrow explicitly.
